items.title: Sidney "Jim Little" Brown Interview, 1960-05-27
items.q: Old man, old man Billy Moran was playing bass at the time. Yeah. And he said, well, I wouldn't learn you how to play bass, boy.

ctx.x: You didn't try to copy after. I'm not trying to say you copied anybody. I just thought maybe you know, like maybe old man Marrero or somebody you might have seen, or Kimball or somebody that you thought

was good. You know, I didn't know who you didn't listen to. Old man, old man Billy Moran was playing bass at the time. Yeah. And he said, well, I wouldn't learn you how to play bass, boy. And, well, well, it was maybe about six or eight months after that I got me a bass, you know, and I started picking around the house. I didn't go around on those guys. I just kept at me home and learned it myself. I didn't try to pick like the other guy. I picked like

Jim Little. Yeah. You had your own style. You could tell that on the old records and from hearing you play. Yeah. I really played that bass. Well, I think that's pretty cool. That, uh, I got one of the records I believe here now, assembled. Your bass method is used right now? Yeah. That's the record we need in, uh, Washington. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. That's, uh, Thomas Ellis. Here's one. That's one. That's Sam Morgan got the bass score here. Yeah. Down in Riverside. Down by Riverside. Everybody's talking about Sammy.…
